- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.15) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions.
- When model shows sharp upward spike followed by downward correction, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is below model by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 2–3 days.
